2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
Respondent Nos.1 to 6, the 1st appellant's father Basavaraj, respondent No.14,
Shadakshari, Maheshwaraiah and Manjunath are the sons and daughters of one Gangappa.
The subject matter of this appeal is land bearing Sy.Nos.48/1 & 125/1 of Hebbal Village, in all, measuring 25 guntas.

Admittedly, the registered Sale Deed of the said property dated 29.11.1979, Ex.P.21 stood in the name of respondent No.1.
NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB
Maheswaraiah
one of the sons of Gangappa
filed O.S.499/1995 before City Civil Court, CCH.7, claiming that Gangappa and all his children constituted joint Hindu family.
It was further contended that, Basavaraj purchased the disputed properties in the name of respondent No.1 Paramashivaiah out of the joint family funds, therefore, that was the joint family property.
Therefore, they are entitled for the share in those properties along with other suit properties.
3. In the said suit, Basavaraj contended that, the said properties were purchased in the name of respondent No.1 Paramashivaiah out of joint family funds, hence joint family properties.
He further contended that there was family partition on 14.03.1996, in which those lands were put for partition and were allotted to his share.
Thereby, they were his absolute properties.
Whereas, respondent No.1 Paramashivaiah contended that he purchased those properties out of his own funds.
4. Pending such suits

Sarvamangala Gowri respondent No.6 herein filed O.S.No.1216/2011 against all her brothers and sisters including Basavaraj for partition and possession of NC:
2023:KHC:25244-DB her 1/12th share claiming that the properties mentioned therein including the Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91318433/
5 subject matter of this appeal are the joint family properties.

sentences.text:
One of the issues in O.S.No.1216/11 was whether Sy.Nos.48/1 and 125/1 in all, measuring 25 guntas, were the self acquired properties of the second defendant i.e. present respondent No.1. O.S.No.1216/2011 and O.S.No.499/1995 and the connected matters were disposed of by the trial Court by judgment and decree on 20.04.2016 holding that Sy.Nos.48/1 and 125/1 were the self acquired properties of Defendant No.2/respondent No.1.
5.

Challenging those findings, the plaintiffs therein filed RFA Nos.1239/2016, 1213/2016,
1379/2016, 769/2022.
They also have challenged the finding in O.S.No.1216/2011 claiming that Sy.Nos.48/1 & 125/1 measuring 25 guntas are not the self acquired properties of respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the appeals filed in RFA Nos.1239/2016, 1213/2016 and 1379/2016 are admitted and pending for hearing.
It is submitted that, there is delay of 6 years in filing RFA No. 769/2022.
It is submitted that the said matter is still at compliance stage and delay is not condoned.

Such being the facts pending of those appeals, Government of Karnataka issued preliminary Notification for acquisition of the disputed properties under KIADB Act for the purpose of Bangalore Metro Rail project.
In the said Notification, respondent No.1 was shown as the owner of the land.
Later on the requisition of appellant No.1 amended Notification dated 16.06.2021 was issued, showing her (Appellant No.1) as the owner of the property.

Soon thereafter, the consent award was passed in favour of appellant No.1.
7.
Respondent No.1 challenged the same before this Court in W.P. 12988/2021 (LA-KIADB).
Ex.P.13 is the order passed in the said writ petition.
By that time, the acquiring bodies had transferred the compensation amount to the account of appellant No.1.
Thereafter, the parties were trapped into another web of litigation.
Criminal case was filed against appellant No.1 and the authorities.
In that criminal case, the account of appellant No.1 to which the amount was transferred was freezed.
8. Respondent Nos.2 to 14 i.e., the sisters and heirs of the sisters got impleaded as the respondents in the said NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB case.
Under Ex.P.13, the learned Single Judge of this Court ordered that, the amount available in the account shall be defreezed and deposited before the City Civil Court.
It was further directed that, the City Civil Court shall deposit the available amount in any nationalised Bank.

The Civil Court was directed to decide the entitlement of the appellants/
respondent No.1 the compensation amount.

It was further directed that the appellant shall give the undertaking before the Civil Court that whatever amount is received by them under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966 shall be re-deposited before the Civil Court, if the petitioner therein succeeds.
9. Thereafter, appellants and respondent Nos.1 to 14 made claim statements before the II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru and they were registered in LAC No. 30/2022.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants gave an undertaking before the trial Court to deposit the entire amount.

The trial Court on recording the evidence, hearing the parties and on examination of the records, passed the impugned award/order holding that the rights of the parties have to be decided in the RFA Nos.1239/2016,
1213/2016, 1379/2016, 799/2022.

The Reference Court directed SLAO to deposit the balance Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91318433/
6 amount - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB and the Bank to deposit the amount pending in defreezed accounts before the Reference Court.

sentences.text: Further, the reference Court by the impugned award directed the appellants to deposit the amount which was not freezed with interest @ 9% within two months, failing which, that shall carry interest @ 15% till the entire amount is deposited.

10. Sri M.Chandrashekar, learned Senior Counsel representing the Advocate for appellant on record tried to make out the case for admission on the following grounds:
i) By the time the order in W.P.No.12988/2021 was passed, the matters were already pending before this Court in RFA Nos. 1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and 769/2022.

When the dispute between the parties was already pending before this Court in Regular First Appeals, there is no scope for reference as Ex.P.13 was unwarranted.
ii) The suits of the plaintiffs in O.S.No.1216/2011 and O.S.No.499/1995 were dismissed and there was no interim stay for such order.

Therefore, the reference Court was in error, in holding that the amount has to be preserved till the disposal of the RFA Nos. 1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB 769/2022.
The reference Court should have abided by the decrees in those suits.

iii) The Reference Court at one stretch says that respondent No.1 is not entitled to the land as he was not in possession, but still calls upon the appellants to deposit the amount, which is incorrect.
iv) In W.P. No. 12988/2021 the order was to deposit only if respondent No.1 succeeds.
Since he was not held to be entitled to the land, the direction under the impugned award for redeposit of the amount is illegal.

11. Sri Harish B.Narasappa, learned Senior Advocate for advocate on record for respondent No.1 opposes the admission on the following grounds:
i) The appellants have committed breach of the interim order of this Court by not furnishing the security for the amount, which was ordered to be re-deposited.
Therefore, under Order XLI Rule 1(3) of CPC the appeal is liable to be dismissed without admission.

- 12 - Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91318433/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB ii)

entities.text: Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The interpretation that the amount was ordered to be deposited, only if, respondent No.1 succeeds is unsustainable as the sisters were later got impleaded in the writ petition and their interests were also required to be decided.

iii) The appellants in the appeal memo seek the prayer, that the impugned award shall be set aside holding that the acquired property is not joint family property and appellants No.2 and 3 alone are entitled for compensation.
But again, states that the matter requires adjudication in RFA Nos.1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and 769/2022.
In view of such prayer itself, the appeal is not maintainable.
iv) The other portions of the same lands were acquired under two other notifications showing respondent No.1 as the land owner and he has received compensation in those cases.
The appellants have not challenged the said orders.
Therefore, it is not open to them to deny the title of respondent No.1 again.
As the rights of the parties have to be decided in RFA Nos.1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and 769/2022 on adjudication this appeal is not maintainable.
vi) The title of the first respondent, in respect of the acquired property was decided in O.S.No.1216/2011, therefore, on that count also the appeal deserves no merit.
vii) The reference Court has passed only a process order to protect the proceeds of acquisition till the substantial rights of parties are decided in the appeals.
For the amount already received, the appellants have not furnished any security.
On that count also the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

12. Sri C.H.Jadhav, learned Senior Counsel for Sri Chetan Jadhav, Advocate on record for respondent No.2, addressing the arguments on the same line, submits that, the statutory authorities released the amount to the appellant unscrupulosly.
Therefore, on that count also, the appeal is not maintainable.

13. Sri K.S.Shivakumara, learned counsel for respondent Nos.6 to 13, Sri Shanmukhappa, learned counsel - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB for respondent No.14, adopt the arguments of learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2.
Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91318433/
8 14.

Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondent No.15-KIADB, Sri N.N.Harish, learned counsel for respondent No.16 submit that the reference Court has not decided the rights of the parties and referred the parties to this Court for adjudication of their rights.
Appeal deserves no merit.
Appellant No.1 said to have released her rights in favour of appellant Nos.2 and 3 under release deed dated 14.7.2008.
Therefore, the appellants' case warrants no admission.
ANALYSIS 15.
Admittedly, for adjudication of the rights of the parties to the disputed property, the matters are pending before this Court in RFA Nos.1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and 769/2022.
Though it was argued about the correctness of the reference in W.P.No.12988/2021 (LA- KIADB), the appellants admittedly challenged the said order in W.A.1291/2021 (LA-KIADB), on the same grounds.
The copy of the judgment dated 19.09.2022 in W.A.No.1291/2021 shows - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB that they withdrew the said appeal.
Therefore it is not open to them to say that reference in Ex.P13 was unwarranted.

16. As rightly pointed out by Sri Harish B.Narasappa, the questions that have to be decided are as "whether the properties are the joint family properties and whether appellant Nos.2 and 3 alone are entitled for compensation?"
Further, the order in W.P.No.12988/2021 has attained finality.
As per the direction in the said case, the undertaking to deposit the amount, if respondent No.1 succeeds still operates.
Admittedly, respondent Nos.2 to 14 got impleaded in the said writ petitions subsequently.
They also claimed interest in the properties.
Apart from that, the appellants themselves seek the prayer for declaration that the suit properties were the joint family properties.
Further, there is a finding in O.S. No.1216/2011 that the said properties are self acquired properties of respondent No.1 and that is still operating against the appellants as well as co-respondents.

Therefore, the sentence in the order in W.P. No.12988/2021(LA-KIADB) cannot be narrowly interpreted to say that the said direction was only with reference to respondent No.1.
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB 17.

Similarly, though the reference Court observed in the impugned order that, 1st respondent was not in possession of the said properties for more than 12 years, therefore, he has lost title, ultimately the Reference Court has held that the matter has to be adjudicated in regular first appeals and the rights of the parties need to be protected till the adjudication is completed.
Such observation itself does not circumvent the order in W.P. No.12988/2021 for deposit of the proceeds.
18. The other important aspect is that, admission of the appeal is not a matter of right.
Conduct of the parties seeking admission of the appeal also becomes relevant.

Though the appellants gave an undertaking that, they would deposit the amount but they have not deposited the amount in Smt. Sunitha vs Sri. G. Paramasivaiah on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91318433/
9 compliance with the impugned award.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this appeal they sought for an interim order.
The impugned award is in the nature of money recovery decree.

Order XLI Rule 1(3) of Civil Procedure Code mandates that in an appeal against decree for payment of money, the appellant shall within such time as the appellate Court may allow, deposit the amount disputed in appeal or furnish such security for such amount.
The default on the part of the appellant in not furnishing the security amounts to - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB violation of the provisions of Order XLI Rule 1(3) of CPC and the order of this Court.

19. Appellant's counsel contends that the interim order of this Court to furnish security is challenged before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, therefore, this Court cannot press into service Order XLI Rule 1(3) of CPC or the conduct of the appellants in not complying that order.
The counsel for the appellants submitted only computer print out in Diary No.27403/2023 claiming that a Special Leave Petition is submitted.
According to the said document the case is not even registered and that is pending only in Diary number.
Therefore, as it is, there is no interim order against the direction of this Court for furnishing the security or vacating the interim order.

20. While questioning the order of the Reference Court, the appellants contend that, as there was no interim order of stay in RFA Nos.1379/2016, 1213/2016, 1239/2016 and 769/2022 and writ petition,
the Reference Court was in error in holding that amount should be preserved pending the aforesaid appeals.

In contrast to that, in this appeal they want this Court to hold its hands on the ground of pendency of Diary - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:25244-DB No.27403/2023 though there is no stay by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
That goes to show that the appellants are blowing hot and cold together and they want to adopt double standards.
That needs to be deprecated.

Non -compliance of Order XLI Rule 1(3) of CPC,
conduct of the appellants and other facts and circumstances discussed above show that it is not a fit case for admission.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
